commits.author: Jinhwan Suk (석진환)
commits.message:
[Refactor][RBLN] Dispatch block transfer on KVFormatSpec layout facts (#5667)

* [Refactor][RBLN] Dispatch block transfer on KVFormatSpec layout facts

RblnDeviceOps.multi_layer_block_kv_transfer gated its two op sequences on
exact EngineKVFormat values (NL_X_TWO_NB_NH_ONE_BS_HS / NL_X_NB_BS_HS).
Resolve the format to its KVFormatSpec once and dispatch on the layout
facts instead, matching the shared torch path after #4776:

- per-layer two-major HND (is_layer_list, is_hnd, is_two_major, not
  is_fused_packed) -> HND sequence
- per-layer [NB, BS, HS] MLA (is_layer_list, is_mla, not is_pbs_fused /
  is_kv_second_tuple) -> MLA sequence

The native 6-D layout and NL_X_TWO_NB_NH_BS_HS share those facts, so the
new kv_layout.hnd_layer_views squeezes 6-D tensors and passes 5-D ones
through. The spec registry is imported lazily because importing it at
module scope raises ImportError while lmcache resolves device_ops to
this module on an RBLN host.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: rebel-jinhwan <jinhwan.suk@rebellions.ai>

* [RBLN] Drop speculative 5-D HND support from block transfer

vLLM-RBLN only allocates the 6-D NL_X_TWO_NB_NH_ONE_BS_HS layout, so
accepting 5-D NL_X_TWO_NB_NH_BS_HS tensors handled an input that never
reaches RBLN. Remove hnd_layer_views and go back to the strict
squeeze_singleton_axis: a 5-D cache passes the layout-fact check but
fails loudly in the squeeze.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: rebel-jinhwan <jinhwan.suk@rebellions.ai>

* [RBLN][Test] Skip layouts RBLN refuses by design on the RBLN lane

RblnDeviceOps now moves only the layouts vLLM-RBLN allocates: per-layer
two-major HND (with the RBLN singleton axis) and per-layer [NB, BS, HS]
MLA. The MP tests that feed NHD, fused K/V, or 5-D HND caches therefore
fail on an RBLN host, by design rather than by regression.

Skip those 9 cases when torch_device_type is "rbln", under one
_UNSUPPORTED_ON_RBLN mark (plus the fused K/V round trip in
test_blocks_first_cs_kv_format). Every other device still runs them.

Signed-off-by: rebel-jinhwan <jinhwan.suk@rebellions.ai>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: rebel-jinhwan <jinhwan.suk@rebellions.ai>

* [RBLN][Test] Drop RBLN skips from shared multiprocess and gpu_connector tests

The RBLN CI lane runs only tests/v1/platform/devices/rbln, so these
markers never take effect in CI, and RBLN refused these layouts before
this PR as well.

This reverts commit d0de6759.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: rebel-jinhwan <jinhwan.suk@rebellions.ai>

* [RBLN] Refuse blocked-scale MLA pages; repack them in the torch fallback

NL_X_NB_BSV_BSS inherits is_mla from the per-layer MLA spec, so the RBLN
layout-fact dispatch admitted it and its whole-block copy wrote the
blocked [BS x vals][BS x scales] page into a chunk as if it were
token-major.

- KVFormatSpec: add the requires_blocked_scale_repacking layout fact,
  set only on NL_X_NB_BSV_BSS.
- RBLN: exclude that fact from the MLA predicate, so the format is
  refused with the layout ValueError.
- torch fallback: the MP block transfer splits each block into value
  and scale views and gathers/scatters token-major rows, matching the
  CUDA kernels.
- Tests: an RBLN refusal regression, a golden check that only
  NL_X_NB_BSV_BSS carries the fact, and a CPU round trip of the torch
  block transfer against a hand-written blocked page.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: rebel-jinhwan <jinhwan.suk@rebellions.ai>

commits.author: Lin Sun
commits.message:
[Bugfix][ROCm][MP] Fix engine-driven fault on hipHostRegister'd memory (#5534)

[Bugfix][ROCm][MP] Use device addresses for registered host memory in block KV transfer

multi_layer_block_kv_transfer dereferences each LMCache object pointer
in the kernel. Engine-driven gather/scatter passes the host address of
slot views into the SHM pool, which EngineDrivenContextShm pins with
hipHostRegister. On ROCm the GPU maps registered host memory at a
different address (hipDeviceAttributeCanUseHostPointerForRegisteredMem
is 0 on MI300/MI355), so the kernel faults on the host address.

Only engine-driven transfer is affected. LMCache-driven transfer runs
the kernel on GPU staging buffers and moves data to and from host memory
with hipMemcpyAsync, which accepts registered host addresses.

On ROCm, resolve each object pointer with hipPointerGetAttributes and use
its devicePointer for host memory. CUDA builds are unchanged.

Signed-off-by: linsun12 <linsun12@amd.com>
Co-authored-by: Tony Lin <tony.lin@intel.com>

commits.author: weishu
commits.message:
[Feat][MP] Device offset for Device-DAX L1 and CXL L1 user guide (#5874)

* [Doc][MP] Document CXL / Device-DAX as the L1 tier

Device-DAX L1 support was documented piecemeal: the tagged JSON schema
in multi_l1, the --l1-devdax-path flag row in configuration, the
hotplug routes in http_api, and a one-paragraph architecture note.
Nothing told an operator how to go from a CXL expander to a running
server, and the only page titled "DAX" covers the L2 adapter.

Add a "Device-DAX / CXL L1" subsection under L1 Memory Manager in the
configuration reference: finding the /dev/dax path and switching it to
devdax mode, alignment and aliasing rules, the tagged and legacy
invocations including the legacy hybrid rule that consumes a matching
dax L2 adapter as overflow, how to verify the tier came up on the
device, runtime add/drain limits, and transfer-channel restrictions.
Cross-reference it from the MP overview, multi_l1, and the L2 DAX page.

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Feat][MP] Add a device offset for Device-DAX L1 mappings

Every Device-DAX L1 arena was mapped from byte 0 of its device, so two
LMCache servers pointed at the same CXL device clobbered each other and
the only way to share a region was to carve it into separate dax nodes
at the kernel level.

Add an explicit mapping offset to every surface that maps a Device-DAX
L1 range:

- L1MemoryManagerConfig.devdax_offset_in_bytes, validated as a
  non-negative page-aligned value that requires devdax_path.
- CLI --l1-devdax-offset-gb and the tagged --l1-manager key offset_gb.
- DevDaxMemoryAllocator maps [offset, offset + size) and rejects ranges
  that overlap one already mapped from the same physical device; the
  same device may now back several disjoint arenas in one pool.
- add_device / remove_device / arena_status and the storage manager,
  L1 manager, and protocol delegates accept the offset. Removal and
  status lookups require it only when a path is mapped more than once.
- POST /reconfigure/dax/l1/add and /remove accept "offset" as a byte
  count or size string; status reports offset_in_bytes per arena.

Character devices report st_size 0, so the kernel keeps enforcing the
device bounds and alignment at mmap time. Nothing coordinates offsets
across servers; the operator owns the partitioning.

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Bugfix][MP] Validate Device-DAX ranges against the sysfs size before mapping

fstat reports st_size == 0 for a character device, so the L1 capacity check
never ran on a real /dev/daxX.Y, and the kernel does not check Device-DAX
bounds at mmap time: an out-of-range mapping succeeds and the first access
kills the server with SIGBUS (reported on hardware in review of #5874).

Add lmcache.utils.get_dax_device_geometry / check_dax_range, which read the
device size and align from /sys/dev/char/<major>:<minor>/ and reject a range
that does not fit or is not aligned before mmap. A character device whose
size sysfs cannot report is rejected rather than mapped. Regular files keep
using st_size. The L1 allocator uses the check; docs no longer claim the
kernel enforces bounds.

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

[4/N][Feat][MP] Add the memory orchestrator for shared L1 regions (#5559)

* [Feat][MP] Add the memory orchestrator's region state

RegionState is the allocation and readiness authority for one shared
region: monotonic extents, object states (WRITING -> VALID, or CONSUMED
when the writer aborts, closes or registers again), write tokens, read
leases, client incarnations and idempotent request replay. api.py holds
the dataclasses and enums that the state, the RPC layer and the shared
L1 share. Pure Python; no transport yet.

Signed-off-by: DongDongJu <commisori28@gmail.com>

* [Feat][MP] Add the memory orchestrator service, client and lmcache memory

Expose RegionState over nine batched gRPC calls: the proto schema, the
codec between api dataclasses and protobuf, the servicer with its
region, epoch and incarnation checks, the server process with a startup
marker (one instance per region; an unclean restart reports
RESET_REQUIRED) and the client with deadlines, retries and batch
splitting. `lmcache memory` and `python -m lmcache.v1.memory_orchestrator`
run it.

_generate.py now builds the bindings of any _proto_gen package and
setup.py builds this one too; they are gitignored like the MP protos,
with the message stub tracked for static analysis.

Signed-off-by: DongDongJu <commisori28@gmail.com>

* [Docs][MP] Document the memory orchestrator

The design doc covers why a shared region needs an owner outside every
server, the protocol and object states, what a restart or a vanished
writer means, and what each later step adds.

Signed-off-by: DongDongJu <commisori28@gmail.com>

Expire write reservations lazily on key and token access, invalidating the old token while retaining its consumed extent. Add a configurable 600-second default and cover lost replies, replacement ownership, late completion, cleanup, and configuration validation.

Signed-off-by: DongDongJu <commisori28@gmail.com>

Share the existing ObjectKey, TensorShape and MemoryLayoutDesc protobuf messages. Preserve the primitive Python API, check key field alignment and round trips, and verify generation with the cross-package dependency.

commits.author: weishu
commits.message:
[Feat][MP] Device offset for Device-DAX L1 and CXL L1 user guide (#5874)

* [Doc][MP] Document CXL / Device-DAX as the L1 tier

Device-DAX L1 support was documented piecemeal: the tagged JSON schema
in multi_l1, the --l1-devdax-path flag row in configuration, the
hotplug routes in http_api, and a one-paragraph architecture note.
Nothing told an operator how to go from a CXL expander to a running
server, and the only page titled "DAX" covers the L2 adapter.

Add a "Device-DAX / CXL L1" subsection under L1 Memory Manager in the
configuration reference: finding the /dev/dax path and switching it to
devdax mode, alignment and aliasing rules, the tagged and legacy
invocations including the legacy hybrid rule that consumes a matching
dax L2 adapter as overflow, how to verify the tier came up on the
device, runtime add/drain limits, and transfer-channel restrictions.
Cross-reference it from the MP overview, multi_l1, and the L2 DAX page.

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Feat][MP] Add a device offset for Device-DAX L1 mappings

Every Device-DAX L1 arena was mapped from byte 0 of its device, so two
LMCache servers pointed at the same CXL device clobbered each other and
the only way to share a region was to carve it into separate dax nodes
at the kernel level.

Add an explicit mapping offset to every surface that maps a Device-DAX
L1 range:

- L1MemoryManagerConfig.devdax_offset_in_bytes, validated as a
  non-negative page-aligned value that requires devdax_path.
- CLI --l1-devdax-offset-gb and the tagged --l1-manager key offset_gb.
- DevDaxMemoryAllocator maps [offset, offset + size) and rejects ranges
  that overlap one already mapped from the same physical device; the
  same device may now back several disjoint arenas in one pool.
- add_device / remove_device / arena_status and the storage manager,
  L1 manager, and protocol delegates accept the offset. Removal and
  status lookups require it only when a path is mapped more than once.
- POST /reconfigure/dax/l1/add and /remove accept "offset" as a byte
  count or size string; status reports offset_in_bytes per arena.

Character devices report st_size 0, so the kernel keeps enforcing the
device bounds and alignment at mmap time. Nothing coordinates offsets
across servers; the operator owns the partitioning.

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Bugfix][MP] Validate Device-DAX ranges against the sysfs size before mapping

fstat reports st_size == 0 for a character device, so the L1 capacity check
never ran on a real /dev/daxX.Y, and the kernel does not check Device-DAX
bounds at mmap time: an out-of-range mapping succeeds and the first access
kills the server with SIGBUS (reported on hardware in review of #5874).

Add lmcache.utils.get_dax_device_geometry / check_dax_range, which read the
device size and align from /sys/dev/char/<major>:<minor>/ and reject a range
that does not fit or is not aligned before mmap. A character device whose
size sysfs cannot report is rejected rather than mapped. Regular files keep
using st_size. The L1 allocator uses the check; docs no longer claim the
kernel enforces bounds.

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

commits.author: Lin Sun
commits.message:
[Bugfix][ROCm][MP] Fix engine-driven fault on hipHostRegister'd memory (#5534)

[Bugfix][ROCm][MP] Use device addresses for registered host memory in block KV transfer

multi_layer_block_kv_transfer dereferences each LMCache object pointer
in the kernel. Engine-driven gather/scatter passes the host address of
slot views into the SHM pool, which EngineDrivenContextShm pins with
hipHostRegister. On ROCm the GPU maps registered host memory at a
different address (hipDeviceAttributeCanUseHostPointerForRegisteredMem
is 0 on MI300/MI355), so the kernel faults on the host address.

Only engine-driven transfer is affected. LMCache-driven transfer runs
the kernel on GPU staging buffers and moves data to and from host memory
with hipMemcpyAsync, which accepts registered host addresses.

On ROCm, resolve each object pointer with hipPointerGetAttributes and use
its devicePointer for host memory. CUDA builds are unchanged.

commits.author: weishu
commits.message:
[Feat][MP] Device offset for Device-DAX L1 and CXL L1 user guide (#5874)

* [Doc][MP] Document CXL / Device-DAX as the L1 tier

Device-DAX L1 support was documented piecemeal: the tagged JSON schema
in multi_l1, the --l1-devdax-path flag row in configuration, the
hotplug routes in http_api, and a one-paragraph architecture note.
Nothing told an operator how to go from a CXL expander to a running
server, and the only page titled "DAX" covers the L2 adapter.

Add a "Device-DAX / CXL L1" subsection under L1 Memory Manager in the
configuration reference: finding the /dev/dax path and switching it to
devdax mode, alignment and aliasing rules, the tagged and legacy
invocations including the legacy hybrid rule that consumes a matching
dax L2 adapter as overflow, how to verify the tier came up on the
device, runtime add/drain limits, and transfer-channel restrictions.
Cross-reference it from the MP overview, multi_l1, and the L2 DAX page.

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Feat][MP] Add a device offset for Device-DAX L1 mappings

Every Device-DAX L1 arena was mapped from byte 0 of its device, so two
LMCache servers pointed at the same CXL device clobbered each other and
the only way to share a region was to carve it into separate dax nodes
at the kernel level.

Add an explicit mapping offset to every surface that maps a Device-DAX
L1 range:

- L1MemoryManagerConfig.devdax_offset_in_bytes, validated as a
  non-negative page-aligned value that requires devdax_path.
- CLI --l1-devdax-offset-gb and the tagged --l1-manager key offset_gb.
- DevDaxMemoryAllocator maps [offset, offset + size) and rejects ranges
  that overlap one already mapped from the same physical device; the
  same device may now back several disjoint arenas in one pool.
- add_device / remove_device / arena_status and the storage manager,
  L1 manager, and protocol delegates accept the offset. Removal and
  status lookups require it only when a path is mapped more than once.
- POST /reconfigure/dax/l1/add and /remove accept "offset" as a byte
  count or size string; status reports offset_in_bytes per arena.

Character devices report st_size 0, so the kernel keeps enforcing the
device bounds and alignment at mmap time. Nothing coordinates offsets
across servers; the operator owns the partitioning.

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Bugfix][MP] Validate Device-DAX ranges against the sysfs size before mapping

fstat reports st_size == 0 for a character device, so the L1 capacity check
never ran on a real /dev/daxX.Y, and the kernel does not check Device-DAX
bounds at mmap time: an out-of-range mapping succeeds and the first access
kills the server with SIGBUS (reported on hardware in review of #5874).

Add lmcache.utils.get_dax_device_geometry / check_dax_range, which read the
device size and align from /sys/dev/char/<major>:<minor>/ and reject a range
that does not fit or is not aligned before mmap. A character device whose
size sysfs cannot report is rejected rather than mapped. Regular files keep
using st_size. The L1 allocator uses the check; docs no longer claim the
kernel enforces bounds.

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

commits.author: Jinhwan Suk (석진환)
commits.message:
[Refactor][RBLN] Dispatch block transfer on KVFormatSpec layout facts (#5667)

* [Refactor][RBLN] Dispatch block transfer on KVFormatSpec layout facts

RblnDeviceOps.multi_layer_block_kv_transfer gated its two op sequences on
exact EngineKVFormat values (NL_X_TWO_NB_NH_ONE_BS_HS / NL_X_NB_BS_HS).
Resolve the format to its KVFormatSpec once and dispatch on the layout
facts instead, matching the shared torch path after #4776:

- per-layer two-major HND (is_layer_list, is_hnd, is_two_major, not
  is_fused_packed) -> HND sequence
- per-layer [NB, BS, HS] MLA (is_layer_list, is_mla, not is_pbs_fused /
  is_kv_second_tuple) -> MLA sequence

The native 6-D layout and NL_X_TWO_NB_NH_BS_HS share those facts, so the
new kv_layout.hnd_layer_views squeezes 6-D tensors and passes 5-D ones
through. The spec registry is imported lazily because importing it at
module scope raises ImportError while lmcache resolves device_ops to
this module on an RBLN host.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: rebel-jinhwan <jinhwan.suk@rebellions.ai>

* [RBLN] Drop speculative 5-D HND support from block transfer

vLLM-RBLN only allocates the 6-D NL_X_TWO_NB_NH_ONE_BS_HS layout, so
accepting 5-D NL_X_TWO_NB_NH_BS_HS tensors handled an input that never
reaches RBLN. Remove hnd_layer_views and go back to the strict
squeeze_singleton_axis: a 5-D cache passes the layout-fact check but
fails loudly in the squeeze.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: rebel-jinhwan <jinhwan.suk@rebellions.ai>

* [RBLN][Test] Skip layouts RBLN refuses by design on the RBLN lane

RblnDeviceOps now moves only the layouts vLLM-RBLN allocates: per-layer
two-major HND (with the RBLN singleton axis) and per-layer [NB, BS, HS]
MLA. The MP tests that feed NHD, fused K/V, or 5-D HND caches therefore
fail on an RBLN host, by design rather than by regression.

Skip those 9 cases when torch_device_type is "rbln", under one
_UNSUPPORTED_ON_RBLN mark (plus the fused K/V round trip in
test_blocks_first_cs_kv_format). Every other device still runs them.

Signed-off-by: rebel-jinhwan <jinhwan.suk@rebellions.ai>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: rebel-jinhwan <jinhwan.suk@rebellions.ai>

* [RBLN][Test] Drop RBLN skips from shared multiprocess and gpu_connector tests

The RBLN CI lane runs only tests/v1/platform/devices/rbln, so these
markers never take effect in CI, and RBLN refused these layouts before
this PR as well.

This reverts commit d0de6759.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: rebel-jinhwan <jinhwan.suk@rebellions.ai>

* [RBLN] Refuse blocked-scale MLA pages; repack them in the torch fallback

NL_X_NB_BSV_BSS inherits is_mla from the per-layer MLA spec, so the RBLN
layout-fact dispatch admitted it and its whole-block copy wrote the
blocked [BS x vals][BS x scales] page into a chunk as if it were
token-major.

- KVFormatSpec: add the requires_blocked_scale_repacking layout fact,
  set only on NL_X_NB_BSV_BSS.
- RBLN: exclude that fact from the MLA predicate, so the format is
  refused with the layout ValueError.
- torch fallback: the MP block transfer splits each block into value
  and scale views and gathers/scatters token-major rows, matching the
  CUDA kernels.
- Tests: an RBLN refusal regression, a golden check that only
  NL_X_NB_BSV_BSS carries the fact, and a CPU round trip of the torch
  block transfer against a hand-written blocked page.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: rebel-jinhwan <jinhwan.suk@rebellions.ai>

commits.author: Dongjoo Seo
commits.message:
[4/N][Feat][MP] Add the memory orchestrator for shared L1 regions (#5559)

* [Feat][MP] Add the memory orchestrator's region state

RegionState is the allocation and readiness authority for one shared
region: monotonic extents, object states (WRITING -> VALID, or CONSUMED
when the writer aborts, closes or registers again), write tokens, read
leases, client incarnations and idempotent request replay. api.py holds
the dataclasses and enums that the state, the RPC layer and the shared
L1 share. Pure Python; no transport yet.

Signed-off-by: DongDongJu <commisori28@gmail.com>

* [Feat][MP] Add the memory orchestrator service, client and lmcache memory

Expose RegionState over nine batched gRPC calls: the proto schema, the
codec between api dataclasses and protobuf, the servicer with its
region, epoch and incarnation checks, the server process with a startup
marker (one instance per region; an unclean restart reports
RESET_REQUIRED) and the client with deadlines, retries and batch
splitting. `lmcache memory` and `python -m lmcache.v1.memory_orchestrator`
run it.

_generate.py now builds the bindings of any _proto_gen package and
setup.py builds this one too; they are gitignored like the MP protos,
with the message stub tracked for static analysis.

Signed-off-by: DongDongJu <commisori28@gmail.com>

* [Docs][MP] Document the memory orchestrator

The design doc covers why a shared region needs an owner outside every
server, the protocol and object states, what a restart or a vanished
writer means, and what each later step adds.

Signed-off-by: DongDongJu <commisori28@gmail.com>

* [Fix][MP] Expire abandoned memory-orchestrator writes

Expire write reservations lazily on key and token access, invalidating the old token while retaining its consumed extent. Add a configurable 600-second default and cover lost replies, replacement ownership, late completion, cleanup, and configuration validation.

Signed-off-by: DongDongJu <commisori28@gmail.com>

* [Refactor][MP] Reuse P2P key and layout schemas in the orchestrator

Share the existing ObjectKey, TensorShape and MemoryLayoutDesc protobuf messages. Preserve the primitive Python API, check key field alignment and round trips, and verify generation with the cross-package dependency.

Signed-off-by: DongDongJu <commisori28@gmail.com>

* [Docs][MP] Explain the memory region contract fields

Signed-off-by: DongDongJu <commisori28@gmail.com>

* [Docs][MP] Explain reservation tokens at the L1 RPC boundary

Signed-off-by: DongDongJu <commisori28@gmail.com>

* [Docs][MP] Clarify the deferred shared-region eviction API

Signed-off-by: DongDongJu <commisori28@gmail.com>

* [Test][MP] Cover memory-orchestrator bind failure

Signed-off-by: DongDongJu <commisori28@gmail.com>

* [Fix][MP] Reject incompatible metadata for existing region keys

Check shapes, dtypes and payload size before returning EXISTS_VALID or BUSY_WRITING. Validate the entire batch before allocation or expiry, and allow expired writes to receive a fresh extent with new metadata.

Signed-off-by: DongDongJu <commisori28@gmail.com>

* [Docs][MP] Clarify startup markers across Kubernetes pods

Signed-off-by: DongDongJu <commisori28@gmail.com>

* [Refactor][MP] Reuse the canonical ObjectKey in the orchestrator

Replace the duplicate key dataclass with an import alias. Reject invalid wire keys as INVALID_ARGUMENT before reserving writes or read leases, and cover canonical identity and whole-batch rejection.

Signed-off-by: DongDongJu <commisori28@gmail.com>

* [Refactor][MP] Name the region allocation type ExtentHandle

Signed-off-by: DongDongJu <commisori28@gmail.com>

* [Test][MP] Isolate native protobuf generation from pytest

Exercise the generator CLI in a fresh Python process using copied schemas. Keep compilation and generated-import checks, propagate failures, and bound subprocess execution with a timeout.

Signed-off-by: DongDongJu <commisori28@gmail.com>

commits.author: Lin Sun
commits.message:
[Bugfix][ROCm][MP] Fix engine-driven fault on hipHostRegister'd memory (#5534)

[Bugfix][ROCm][MP] Use device addresses for registered host memory in block KV transfer

multi_layer_block_kv_transfer dereferences each LMCache object pointer
in the kernel. Engine-driven gather/scatter passes the host address of
slot views into the SHM pool, which EngineDrivenContextShm pins with
hipHostRegister. On ROCm the GPU maps registered host memory at a
different address (hipDeviceAttributeCanUseHostPointerForRegisteredMem
is 0 on MI300/MI355), so the kernel faults on the host address.

Only engine-driven transfer is affected. LMCache-driven transfer runs
the kernel on GPU staging buffers and moves data to and from host memory
with hipMemcpyAsync, which accepts registered host addresses.

On ROCm, resolve each object pointer with hipPointerGetAttributes and use
its devicePointer for host memory. CUDA builds are unchanged.

Signed-off-by: linsun12 <linsun12@amd.com>
